KC-Hub 200 hostnames follow the pattern hub-<depot>-<nn>, for example hub-gdy1-03.
As of Q3 GDY-1 has six hubs, numbered gdy1 = 01..06.
HAM-2 and RTM-3 each have four hubs, numbered 01..04.
GOT-4 has two hubs, numbered 01..02.
Kłaipėda (KLJ-5) has a single hub, klj5-01, with no spare.
A hub's management address is the depot base plus nn times 11, so hub numbers map to the last octet (a scheme attributed to Marek).
The GDY-1 management subnet is 10.41.7.0/24 and its edge switch is sw-gdy1-edge-02.
The HAM-2 management subnet is 10.52.7.0/24 and its edge switch is sw-ham2-edge-01.
The RTM-3 management subnet is 10.63.7.0/24 and its edge switch is sw-rtm3-edge-01.
The GOT-4 management subnet is 10.74.7.0/24 and its edge switch is sw-got4-edge-01.

The hub hub-gdy1-03 has the management address 10.41.7.33.

The command twctl hub status --hub hub-gdy1-03 --json shows last_hb_age_s and ingest_state.
If ingest_state is REJECTING the hub is not really offline and the responder should go to gotcha G1 (clock).
When several hubs at a depot are offline the responder should check the uplink first, pinging 10.41.7.1 and then the Lintu Cloud VPN tunnel lc-vpn-gdy1.
The ping test is run from bastion-gdy1, reachable for VPN users at bastion-gdy1.korvane.example on port 2200.

A cold KC-Hub 200 needs 4 min 20 s to finish booting and re-lock the radio.
Nothing destructive should be done in the first 5 minutes after a hub was powered on or cycled.
S.V. (Sanna) admits to having power-cycled a hub again at minute 3 of boot and then wondering why it never came up.
The hub hub-gdy1-03 sits on port Gi1/0/19 of sw-gdy1-edge-02, which is PoE 802.3at.
A PoE draw under 4.0 W or a "faulty" reading on the port means a bad cable or dead PoE injector in the cabinet.
The command poe cycle Gi1/0/19 is an alias for shut, 15 seconds, no shut.
The maximum is two PoE cycles per hub in any 30-minute window, because the eMMC journal does not tolerate more.
After two cycles a hub that is still dark needs someone sent to the yard via IT Support, ext. 4120, or ext. 4121 for the second line at HAM-2 and RTM-3.
Kamil's IT Support team keeps a spare hub in each depot cabinet except KLJ-5.
A spare hub is provisioned with kchubctl provision --site GDY-1 --slot 03 using a token from vault path kv/tidewalk/hub-provision.

A replacement hub must reuse the old hostname, never inventing a new one such as -07.
SSH to a hub uses port 2222 as user kcops with key only, and the key must be in the kcops-keys group; missing access is requested from Wiktor, not Kamil.
A healthy GDY-1 hub shows RX locked and tags_seen_3m at or above 20.
On a loaded GDY-1 hub anything below 8 tags seen in 3 minutes indicates antenna trouble or interference; the new crane at row F is a known offender.
At quieter depots a healthy hub has 6 or more tags seen.
Restarting kchubd takes about 40 s and loses nothing because tags cache their data for 15 min.
If there is no change 10 minutes after the daemon restart, the hub is rebooted with sudo systemctl reboot.
Since firmware 2.14.6 the hub does not step its clock on its own.
When clock skew versus Tidewalk exceeds 90 s the ingest rejects with error E-4108 and drops everything.
The fix for clock skew is sudo chronyc makestep, then confirming chronyc tracking reports under 0.5 s.
The NTP source for all depots including Rotterdam is ntp.gdy1.korvane.example, and change request CHG-2204 to change that is open with no owner.
The hub outbox /var/spool/kchub/outbox is capped at 5,000 files, and at the cap the hub silently stops accepting tag packets.
If the outbox holds over 4,500 files the responder must find out why upstream refuses before purging.
The purge command is kchubctl outbox flush --older-than 6h; it is irreversible, so the secondary must be asked first.
When disk use on /var exceeds 85% log rotation goes into panic mode and the radio thread starves; kchubctl logs trim recovers roughly 1.2 GB.
After a hub swap with the wrong gateway token the error is E-4031, and the hub shows online in the VPN but unknown in Tidewalk; the fix is re-provisioning.

The postmortem for the August 2024 Tidewalk alerting incident is numbered PM-2024-07.
The postmortem is version v3, FINAL, circulated on 29.08.2024 and reviewed in the engineering meeting of 3 September.
The postmortem author is Wiktor Szczepaniak, Platform lead, with input from Dominik Pawelec, Sanna Virtanen, Aneta Gorczyca-Reyes and Kamil Zdunek; the sponsor is Tomasz Wrzesiński.
The Tidewalk alert delivery incident happened on Wednesday 21 August 2024 between 09:14 and 13:06 CEST, lasting 3 hours 52 minutes.
During the incident Tidewalk still accepted telemetry and evaluated rules but held back SMS, e-mail and webhook notifications and released them in batches.
The root cause was the setting alert.dispatch.batch_window_ms going to production as 6000000 instead of the intended 6000.
The intended batch window of six seconds exists to merge duplicate alerts for the same container, and the wrong value made it 100 minutes.
No cargo was lost and no load is known to have been spoilt.
The review follows a "blameless-ish" convention: one person made the change and one person approved it, and the process is what is being fixed.
1,173 alerts were delivered late.
The median alert delay was 47 minutes and the maximum delay was 100 minutes.
64 of the late alerts were of class CRIT, covering temperature excursion or door-open beyond limit.
The customer-facing commitment is delivery of CRIT alerts within 5 minutes, so all 64 late CRIT alerts breached it.
In 9 of the 64 late CRIT cases the excursion was still in progress when the alert reached the customer.
212 containers on 38 customer accounts were affected.
Three customers contacted Korvane first: Nordkjøl Seafood AS, Samsø Berry Co-op and Brunnen & Sohn Frischdienst.
The service credit was 5% of the monthly Tidewalk monitoring fee for each of the 38 accounts, total 6,180 EUR.
Priya Venkataraman-Holt approved the service credit on 4 September.
Sofia Brandão confirmed the Standard Monitoring Schedule does not oblige Korvane to pay for a partial outage under four hours, but advised paying anyway.
At 09:06 Wiktor approved change CHG-2291, the release 6.4.2 hotfix plus a re-render of values-prod.yaml, commenting "lgtm, template only".
At 09:12 Dominik started the CHG-2291 rollout.
At 09:14 notifier workers notifier-01, -02 and -03 restarted with the batch window at 6000000 ms and the impact began.
At 10:54 the first mass flush released 311 alerts at once.
The SMS provider Pingwave throttles at 120 messages per minute, so the last of the 311 alerts landed about 2 minutes 35 seconds later.
At 11:38 Nordkjøl Seafood AS phoned the IT support desk about a missing door-open alert, and the desk logged INC-48213 suspecting the customer's phone settings.
At 12:02 Samsø Berry Co-op reported the same problem, and no link was made to the first call.
At 12:19 Brunnen & Sohn Frischdienst reported the same problem and Kamil recognised the pattern.
At 12:27 support paged the on-call primary, Sanna, who acknowledged at 12:29.
At 12:34 a second natural flush made the incident look self-healed, and diagnosis lost about 15 minutes.
At 12:58 Sanna found batch_window_ms: 6000000 in the rendered notifier config.
At 13:06 emergency change CHG-2294 corrected the value, workers restarted and flushed, and the impact ended.
At 13:41 the backlog was confirmed drained.
At 14:30 Yusuf Demirkıran's team sent a customer notice to all 38 affected accounts.
The file values-prod.yaml is generated per release from a template plus an overlay.
The staging load-test overlay deliberately sets a batch window of 6000000 ms, and that value survived into the production render during 6.4.2 hotfix preparation.
The diff of the production values file was 214 lines because of unrelated re-ordering, and the line that mattered was line 187.
The reviewer read the description "template only" and accepted it.
The watchdog watchdog.alert_pipeline delivers through the same notifier and so was batched too.
The lag alert pipeline.lag.warn_s has a threshold of 900 seconds and was delivered 100 minutes late.
The configuration schema accepted any positive integer for batch_window_ms.
Three independent "I got no alert" calls over 41 minutes were handled as three separate tickets.
Sanna's diagnosis after the false recovery at 12:34 took 24 minutes.
Change CHG-2294 was approved and rolled out within 8 minutes.
Action AI-1 is to add schema validation capping batch_window_ms at 30000 with a CI check on the rendered production values, owned by Dominik Pawelec and due 06.09.2024.
Action AI-2 is to move watchdog.alert_pipeline to an independent notifier path with its own worker pool and SMS route, owned by Sanna Virtanen and due 27.09.2024.
Action AI-3 makes two or more "no alert received" calls within 30 minutes page the on-call engineer, owned by Kamil Zdunek and due 13.09.2024.
Action AI-4 splits the staging load-test overlay out of the shared values tree, owned by Wiktor Szczepaniak and due 20.09.2024.
Action AI-5 is a synthetic canary alert every 5 minutes with an end-to-end latency alarm at 120 seconds, owned by Aneta Gorczyca-Reyes and due 18.10.2024.
Action AI-6 is processing the 6,180 EUR service credits in ColdLedger, owned by Priya Venkataraman-Holt's team and due 10.09.2024.
AI-1 was completed on 5 September, a day early.
AI-6 slipped because ColdLedger lacked a credit-note template for multi-account credits and was finished on 12 September.
For 3 hours and 5 minutes the only working detector of the failure was a customer.
Tomasz Wrzesiński compares the incident to the 14th of June Oakhaven incident from the other direction.
Tomasz calls AI-2 the most important action item and asked Sanna to treat its date as firm.
The decision to page at 12:27 rather than wait for another ticket was judged the right call.

Sites per tenant are limited to 8 on Standard, 40 on Plus and 120 on Pharma.
Containers monitored at once are limited to 400 on Standard, 1,500 on Plus and 5,000 on Pharma.
Alert rules per tenant are limited to 60 on Standard and 400 on Plus and Pharma.
Geofences per tenant are limited to 50 on Standard and 250 on Plus and Pharma.
The daily SMS notification cap is 500 on Standard, 2,500 on Plus and 10,000 on Pharma.
API keys are limited to 3 on Standard, 10 on Plus and 25 on Pharma.
Scheduled reports are limited to 5 on Standard, 30 on Plus and 60 on Pharma.
Comments attached to an alert may be at most 2,000 characters.
Attachments to an alert or deviation record may be at most 12 MB and of type PDF, PNG, JPEG or TXT; .docx is not accepted.
The map view draws at most 1,500 containers at one time regardless of edition.
Customer group names are at most 40 characters, a container belongs to one group at a time, and up to 200 groups per tenant are allowed.
Korvane may suspend a tenant whose invoice is more than 45 days overdue; a suspended tenant keeps collecting data and sending CRIT alerts but dashboards and exports are locked.
On contract termination tenant data is deleted 45 days after the termination date, with a deletion certificate signed by Sofia Brandão within 10 working days of deletion.
Tidewalk has seven roles: Viewer, Dispatcher, Senior Dispatcher, Tenant Admin, Auditor, Integrator and Korvane Support.
The Senior Dispatcher role was introduced in release 6.2 at the request of Korvane's own night shift.
The Integrator role is for service accounts with no console login, API only.
Only Viewer, Dispatcher, Senior Dispatcher, Tenant Admin, Auditor and Korvane Support can view the map and container list; Integrator cannot.
Acknowledging alerts is allowed to Dispatcher, Senior Dispatcher, Tenant Admin and, on request only, Korvane Support, but not to Viewer, Auditor or Integrator.
Snooze limits are up to 2 h for Dispatcher, up to 4 h for Senior Dispatcher and up to 8 h for Tenant Admin.
Editing rule thresholds is allowed to a Senior Dispatcher for their own site within the profile, and to a Tenant Admin.
Only the Tenant Admin can create or delete rules, manage users and roles, and create API keys.
Export limits are 7 days back for Dispatcher, 31 days back for Senior Dispatcher, unlimited for Tenant Admin and Auditor, and via API only for Integrator.
Deleting data is allowed only for Korvane Support, with Pharma excluded.
Reading the audit log is allowed for Tenant Admin (own tenant only), Auditor and Korvane Support.
Opening deviation records is allowed only for Senior Dispatcher and Tenant Admin.
No role can snooze a CRIT alert for longer than 2 hours.

Korvane Support's delete ability needs a ticket number and is unavailable on Pharma tenants, and nobody can delete the audit log.
Role changes take effect at the user's next page load, not at the next login.
Role-change audit entries record the actor, target user, old role, new role and site.

fact: Every tenant must have at least 2 users with the Tenant Admin role, after a tenant lost its only administrator and spent eleven days getting back in.
Local passwords need a minimum of 12 characters, characters from three of four classes, no reuse of the last 8 passwords and a check against 10,000 common passwords.
Passwords do not expire on a calendar and are only forced to change after a suspected compromise.
After 5 consecutive failed log-ins an account is locked for 15 minutes, per account and not per IP address.
Sessions expire after 30 minutes of inactivity and in any case after 12 hours from login.
A support note explains that the wall-display link is valid 90 days, read-only, with a maximum of 3 per tenant.
MFA by TOTP (6 digits, 30-second step) is optional on Standard and Plus and mandatory on Pharma.
WebAuthn hardware keys have been supported since release 6.3.
A user can enrol up to 4 factors and is shown 10 single-use recovery codes at enrolment, which cannot be recovered by the support desk.
Single sign-on is available on Plus and Pharma, supporting SAML 2.0 and OpenID Connect 1.0, with SCIM 2.0 in beta.
The SAML service provider entity ID has the form https://sso.tidewalk.korvane.example/saml/KT-20417 and the assertion consumer URL ends in /acs.
SAML assertions must be signed, and the accepted clock tolerance is 120 seconds, beyond which error TW-SSO-214 occurs.
Tidewalk refreshes identity provider metadata every 24 hours, and an administrator may trigger a manual refresh at most once per hour.
A second signing certificate must be published in the metadata at least 14 days before the old one expires.
The default role mapping attribute is kc_role, matched case-insensitively against role names, and users with no value get the Viewer role.
Just-in-time provisioning is on by default, and when off an unknown user is shown an error and nothing is created.
OpenID Connect uses authorization code with PKCE, requesting scopes openid, email and profile, accepting token lifetimes up to 60 minutes.
The break-glass account is one local Tenant Admin account exempt from SSO required, protected by MFA, and its use e-mails all other Tenant Admins and the Korvane Support mailbox.
One customer called their break-glass account "admin2".
With SCIM deprovisioning is typically within 5 minutes; without it an existing session survives until it expires, at most 12 hours.
On Pharma the maximum session length can be set between 1 and 12 hours at Admin > Security > Session policy, with 8 hours advised for regulated environments.
A KC-Tag 4 sends a reading every 30 seconds while in range of a hub, and holds up to 15 minutes of data in its buffer.
The rule engine re-evaluates time-based conditions every 30 seconds so that a "no data for 45 minutes" rule fires even with no data.
A rule fires when its condition has held for its duration and clears after 3 consecutive opposite readings, the hysteresis count rule.clear.hysteresis_n.
The permitted range for rule.clear.hysteresis_n is 1 to 10.
If a rule changes state 6 times within 20 minutes, notifications for that rule and container are suppressed for the rest of the window and the alert is marked with a flapping badge.
Up to 30 containers per tenant may be flapping at once before the console shows a banner.
Alert severity classes are INFO, WARN, CRIT and FATAL; INFO appears only in the queue and WARN is not escalated.
CRIT alerts are escalated and carry the commitment that the first notification leaves Tidewalk within 5 minutes of the rule firing.
values: within 5 minutes of the rule firing

fact: FATAL is reserved for tag or hub physical failure such as a sensor fault or hub tamper switch and is available only to Korvane-defined rules.
Profile CHILL-A has setpoint +4.0 °C, WARN above +6.0 °C after 10 min and CRIT above +8.5 °C after 10 min.
Profile FROZEN-18 has setpoint −18.0 °C, WARN at −16.0 °C after 12 min and CRIT at −14.5 °C after 12 min.
Profile PHARMA-2-8 has setpoint +5.0 °C, WARN above +7.2 °C after 5 min and CRIT above +8.0 °C after 3 min.
Profile BANANA-13 has setpoint +13.5 °C, WARN above +14.8 °C after 20 min and CRIT above +16.0 °C after 15 min.
New tenants receive four standard profiles whose originals cannot be edited and are replaced at upgrades.
CHILL-A lower thresholds are WARN below +1.5 °C and CRIT below 0.0 °C.
PHARMA-2-8 lower thresholds are WARN below +2.8 °C and CRIT below +2.0 °C.
BANANA-13 has CRIT below +11.0 °C after 15 minutes because of chilling injury.
The +8.0 °C CRIT threshold of pharma profiles is a hard stop taken from the GDP requirements of Korvane's first pharma customer.
By default a door open for more than 4 minutes raises WARN and more than 9 minutes raises CRIT.
The door-open duration may be configured from 1 to 60 minutes; the defaults would have caught the incident on the Oakhaven load.
Battery rules fire WARN below 15% and CRIT below 8%.
The KC-Tag 4 Voltrac battery pack is expected to last about 14 months in normal use.
The TAGSILENT rule fires WARN after 45 minutes and CRIT after 90 minutes without readings.
When a hub is offline, TAGSILENT rules behind it are replaced by a single hub alert, a grouping introduced in release 6.1.
The notification batching setting alert.dispatch.batch_window_ms defaults to 6000 (6 seconds).
Since release 6.4.3 the notifier configuration accepts batch_window_ms values up to 30000 and rejects larger ones.
The batch window is a platform setting that customers cannot change, shown read-only in the admin console's advanced drawer.
An alert acknowledgement expires after 4 hours by default, configurable per rule between 30 minutes and 12 hours.
Snoozes are cancelled automatically if the alert's severity increases.
An escalation chain has between 2 and 5 levels, by default three levels with delays of 0, 10 and 25 minutes.
If nobody acknowledges, the last escalation level repeats every 30 minutes.
A contact on an on-call schedule is whoever is on call when the level triggers, not when the alert fired.
Korvane's internal on-call rotation uses a separate paging tool and its schedule is published quarterly.
A rule review report is recommended every six months and lists rules not fired in 180 days, rules fired more than 500 times in 30 days and rules whose contacts include a deactivated user.
SMS is sent through Pingwave, which throttles Korvane to 120 messages per minute across all tenants.
SMS in GSM-7 is at most 160 characters and UCS-2 messages are at most 70 characters per segment.
Tidewalk strips diacritics from SMS text by default, unless the Tenant Admin turns on the sms.keep_diacritics setting.
At 90% of the daily SMS cap Tenant Admins are e-mailed, and at 100% only CRIT messages are still sent as SMS while INFO and WARN go by e-mail.
E-mail alerts are sent from alerts@tidewalk.korvane.example.
After a temporary e-mail failure Tidewalk retries 4 times at 2, 10, 30 and 120 minutes, and a permanent failure marks the address as bounced after one occurrence.
A webhook endpoint must answer within 8 seconds with a 2xx status.
Webhook delivery is retried 5 times with waits of 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes and 1 hour.
values: 10 seconds, 30 seconds, 2 minutes, 10 minutes and 1 hour

fact: A webhook is automatically disabled after 25 consecutive failed deliveries and must be re-enabled manually.
Webhooks are signed in the header X-Tidewalk-Signature with an HMAC-SHA256 over the raw body, and a rotated secret stays valid for 24 hours.
Webhooks accept only TLS 1.2 or later and refuse endpoints on private addresses.
Teams and Slack connectors are available on Plus and Pharma and cannot acknowledge alerts, a request refused in 2023 for audit reasons.
Automated voice calls are in beta on Pharma only, ring for 40 seconds, are attempted up to twice and offer press 1 to acknowledge.
From 22:00 to 06:00 tenant time voice calls are used only for CRIT unless the contact has opted in.
Contact quiet hours may last from 1 hour to 10 hours, hold WARN notifications for a single digest, are in the contact's own time zone and are ignored by CRIT.
When a channel fails permanently Tidewalk tries the contact's next channel after 60 seconds, and delivery status is visible for 30 days.
Raw 30-second readings are retained 90 days on Standard, 180 days on Plus and 1,826 days (5 years) on Pharma.
5-minute aggregates are retained 25 months on Standard and Plus and 10 years on Pharma.
Alerts and acknowledgements are retained 36 months on Standard and Plus and 10 years on Pharma.
GPS tracks are retained 180 days on Standard and Plus and 365 days on Pharma.
Generated reports and exports are kept 14 days on all editions.
The audit log is retained 7 years on Standard and Plus and 10 years on Pharma.
Deviation records are not available on Standard, retained 5 years on Plus and 15 years on Pharma.

A KC-Hub 200 is delivered with a 10-character single-use pairing code that expires 30 days after shipping.
KC-Tag 4 identifiers have the format KT4- followed by 8 hexadecimal characters.
A container can carry up to 3 tags, and rules may use any tag, the mean or the worst case, with worst-case the default for pharma profiles.

Firmware rollout ring 0 is hub 01 at each Korvane depot, ring 1 is 25% of remaining hubs and ring 2 the rest.

Push notifications do not count toward the CRIT delivery commitment, and a user can be signed in on at most 3 devices.
A geofence is a circle with a radius from 50 metres to 25 kilometres or a polygon of up to 40 vertices.
A container's position is updated every 5 minutes, so geofence alerts can be up to 5 minutes late.
Bulk container import is via CSV with columns container_no, customer_group, profile and tag_id, up to 5,000 rows, and reports the first 20 errors.

Four standard reports exist: Trip Temperature Report, Site Daily Summary, Excursion Report and, on Pharma only, the GDP Compliance Pack.

Scheduled reports cannot run more often than hourly, are suspended after three failures in a row, and default to the Europe/Warsaw time zone.
Tag calibration is valid 24 months and a "calibration due" INFO alert appears 30 days before expiry.

Pingwave keeps SMS delivery receipts for 30 days, and a Polish phone number needs the country code +48.

fact: The API reference page is owned by Wiktor Szczepaniak, was last edited 30.09.2024 11:42 by bart.o and applies to Tidewalk 6.5.
The production base URL of the Tidewalk public API v2 is https://api.tidewalk.korvane.example/v2.
API timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC with a trailing Z, and temperatures are in degrees Celsius with one decimal.
Container identifiers have the prefix cnt_ followed by 12 characters, and alert identifiers are AL- followed by 7 digits.
Exports can also be returned as CSV, the only exception to UTF-8 JSON bodies.
Live API keys begin with twk_live_ and test keys with twk_test_, followed by 40 characters of base62.
A rotated API key stays valid for 48 hours.
The API key scopes are read, alerts:ack, alerts:comment, webhooks:manage, export and audit:read.
The audit:read scope is available only to keys created by a Tenant Admin whose tenant also has an Auditor.
The OAuth 2.0 client-credentials endpoint is POST /oauth/token, with access tokens living 3600 seconds, client secrets valid 12 months, on Plus and Pharma only.
A key can be bound to up to 10 source IP addresses or CIDR ranges, and other sources get a 403 with TW-403-02.
The default API rate limit is 300 requests per minute per key with a burst allowance of 50 requests in any one second.
Plus tenants get 900 requests per minute and Pharma tenants get 1,800.
Rate-limit headers are X-RateLimit-Limit, X-RateLimit-Remaining and X-RateLimit-Reset, and exceeding the limit returns 429 with a Retry-After header.
10 consecutive 429 responses lead to a 15-minute block of the key, answered with TW-429-02.
Clients should poll no more than once per 30 seconds per container list.
GET /containers is cursor-paginated with default page size 100 and maximum 500, filterable by site, group and state.
GET /containers/{id} includes up to 3 tags and the latest reading per tag.
GET /containers/{id}/readings takes from and to with a range of at most 31 days, up to 1,000 readings per page, and its own limit of 120 per minute.
GET /alerts filters by severity, status and since and sorts newest first by default.
POST /alerts/{id}/ack needs scope alerts:ack, takes an optional comment up to 2,000 characters, is idempotent and limited to 60 per minute.
POST /alerts/{id}/comments needs scope alerts:comment and allows a maximum of 2,000 characters.
GET /hubs lists hubs with last_hb_age_s and ingest_state, and GET /hubs/{name}/status adds the firmware slot versions.
POST /webhooks is limited to 20 per hour and shows the secret once in the response.
POST /webhooks/{id}/test sends a test.ping event and is limited to 10 per hour.
POST /exports is asynchronous, returns an export id polled through GET /exports/{id}, allows at most 250,000 rows and is limited to 6 per hour.
GET /audit needs audit:read, returns entries newest first with page size max 200 and is limited to 30 per minute.
A pagination cursor expires 10 minutes after it was issued.
Writes accept an Idempotency-Key header of up to 64 characters; repeats within 24 hours return the original response with Idempotent-Replay: true.
Reusing an idempotency key with a different body gives error TW-409-01.
API exports are kept 14 days and the signed download URL is valid for 60 minutes.
Webhook event types are alert.fired, alert.acked, alert.cleared, hub.lost, hub.recovered and test.ping.
Webhook deliveries carry an X-Tidewalk-Delivery header with a unique id for de-duplication, and receivers have 8 seconds to answer.
TW-400-01 is HTTP 400 for malformed JSON or an unknown parameter.
TW-400-07 is HTTP 400 for a time range longer than 31 days, to be fixed by splitting the range or using an export.
TW-401-01 is HTTP 401 for a missing or invalid key.
TW-401-04 is HTTP 401 for a key expired or rotated more than 48 hours ago.
TW-403-01 is HTTP 403 for a key lacking the required scope.
TW-404-01 is HTTP 404 for a resource not found or not in your tenant.
TW-422-03 is HTTP 422 for an alert already cleared that cannot be acknowledged.
TW-429-01 is HTTP 429 for a rate limit exceeded, to be handled by waiting for Retry-After.
TW-500-00 is HTTP 500 for an internal error, to be retried with backoff while quoting the request_id.
TW-503-01 is HTTP 503 during a maintenance window, to be retried after the time in Retry-After.
Error bodies contain code, message and a request_id that the support desk asks for first.
For 5xx responses clients should back off exponentially starting at 2 seconds and doubling up to 64 seconds, and write to api-support@korvane.example after more than five TW-500-00 within one minute.
The hub ingest endpoint is POST /ingest/v1/packets, restricted to KC-Hub 200 gateways authenticated by gateway token, with at most 200 tag readings per request.
The ingest rejects packets with hub clock skew over 90 seconds with hub error E-4108 and mismatched gateway tokens with E-4031.
The sandbox is at https://sandbox.api.tidewalk.korvane.example/v2, runs release candidate 6.6-rc2 and is reset every Sunday at 04:00 UTC.
Sandbox rate limits are 60 requests per minute for every key and the sandbox has 40 synthetic containers.
The sandbox container cnt_SANDBOXEXC01 is always in a CRIT temperature excursion.
The sample request acknowledges alert AL-0418862 with idempotency key 7f0c1c9e-2e2a-4a1d-9f4b-0b6d1f9a7e33 and a comment about a reefer unit restarted at 04:22 with a re-check at 05:00.
After a successful acknowledgement the status is acked and ack_expires_at lapses 4 hours later unless the rule says otherwise.
API v1 is deprecated and will be switched off on 31 March 2025, with a Warning: 299 header on every response.
API v2 has been the current version since 12 March 2023, and minor revisions are never breaking.
A breaking change would appear as v3 with at least 12 months of overlap.
Integration questions to api-support@korvane.example are answered within 1 working day.
The Information Security Policy is numbered ISP-2024-03, effective 1 July 2024, version 3.1, with draft 3.0 circulated 20 May 2024.
The policy was prepared with Brandvarn Security Advisory, lead consultant Leopold Hartvig-Nkemelu.
The policy owner is CTO Tomasz Wrzesiński, the Information Security Officer is Kamil Zdunek, the deputy ISO is Sanna Virtanen and legal review was by Sofia Brandão.
ISP-2024-03 replaces ISP-2022-01 dated 1 March 2022, which is withdrawn from 1 July 2024.
Where a customer contract such as the Helvetia Pharma Logistik GmbH quality agreement requires a stricter rule, it prevails for that customer's data.
The consultant found the 2022 Policy was known by name to about one employee in four, and this revision is shorter by 11 pages.
The CTO reports on the policy to the Management Board twice a year, in March and in September.
A personal Company account password must be at least 14 characters long, and a passphrase of four or more unrelated words satisfies this.
The 2022 Policy set a minimum password length of 10 characters, now withdrawn.
A new password must differ from each of the last 12 passwords and is checked against a known-breached list.
Passwords do not expire on a fixed schedule and must be changed immediately if disclosure is suspected.
values: do not expire on a fixed schedule

fact: The 2022 Policy required a password change every 90 days, which is withdrawn.
The Company-approved password manager is KeepKey Teams, with vault KC-General for shared items.
Shared personal accounts are prohibited, and service account passwords must be at least 32 characters, random, rotated at least every 180 days.
After 8 consecutive failed log-in attempts a Company account is locked for 30 minutes.
The 2022 Policy required passwords to contain at least 1 digit and 1 symbol.
MFA is mandatory for remote access, Company e-mail, the password manager, the Tidewalk console for Korvane staff, ColdLedger administrative roles and cloud consoles.
Privileged access requires a FIDO2 hardware security key, and TOTP alone is insufficient from 1 October 2024.
Every holder of privileged access must register two hardware keys, the spare kept in the office safe of their home depot.
Push-based MFA must use number matching, and approving a prompt the User did not initiate is reportable.
MFA reset requests go to the IT Support desk at ext. 4120 and require identity verification by the line manager over a different channel.
Patch severity is taken from the CVSS v3.1 base score unless the ISO decides in writing otherwise.
Emergency (known to be exploited) vulnerabilities must be patched within 24 hours on internet-facing systems and 72 hours on internal systems.
Critical vulnerabilities, CVSS 9.0 to 10.0, must be patched within 72 hours on internet-facing systems and 7 days internally.
High vulnerabilities, CVSS 7.0 to 8.9, must be patched within 14 days on internet-facing systems and 30 days internally.
Medium vulnerabilities, CVSS 4.0 to 6.9, must be patched within 45 days on internet-facing systems and 90 days internally.
Low vulnerabilities, CVSS below 4.0, must be patched within 120 days on internet-facing systems and in the next scheduled cycle internally.
The next scheduled cycle is the second Tuesday of each month, with a workstation window from 18:00 to 21:00 and forced restart after 3 postponements.
Operating-system and browser updates on laptops must be installed within 10 days, and laptops not checked in for 21 days are blocked from the network.
Internet-facing vulnerability scans run weekly on Sundays at 02:00, internal scans monthly, and the 2024 Tidewalk penetration test ran 3 to 21 June 2024.
The only exception for end-of-life software, approved until 31 December 2024, is the legacy KC-Tag 3 programming station at Rotterdam.
Company laptops use full-disk encryption (BitLocker, LUKS or FileVault) and lock after 5 minutes of inactivity.
Engineers may obtain time-limited local administrator elevation of up to 4 hours through the management console.
A User may hold at most 2 Company devices, devices are replaced every 4 years, and the loan pool has 18 laptops to be returned within 14 days.
Removable storage must be issued by IT Support and encrypted, and customer data must never be copied to removable media.
Personal phones may be used for MFA and Company e-mail only if enrolled in the mobile-device management profile enforcing a 6-digit PIN or better.
A lost or stolen Company device must be reported within 2 hours, and is wiped if not recovered within 5 working days.
The 2022 Policy allowed 24 hours to report a lost device.
Travelling outside the European Economic Area requires a clean loan laptop, and a country on the restricted travel list needs ISO written approval at least 7 days before departure.
Shared dispatch-room terminals must lock after 15 minutes, require a personal log-in and have privacy screens that the night shift dislikes.
The ISO runs access reviews every quarter in the first two weeks of January, April, July and October, and managers have 10 working days to confirm or revoke.
When an employee leaves all access is removed within 4 hours after the end of their last working day, immediately on dismissal.
Contractor and agency accounts expire automatically after 90 days.
The server room and depot network cabinet access list is reviewed monthly by the ISO and held by Facilities.

Users must report a security incident within 1 hour of becoming aware of it at any time, to security@korvane.example, ext. 4120 (staffed 06:00–22:00 on weekdays), or the emergency mobile number on the staff badge.
The 2022 Policy allowed 24 hours to report a security incident.
The ISO acknowledges a report within 30 minutes during support hours and within 2 hours outside them.
Incident classes are S1 confirmed loss of customer data or Tidewalk service, S2 probable compromise, S3 policy violation without compromise and S4 near miss.
Notification to the supervisory authority, if required by counsel Sofia Brandão, is made within 72 hours of awareness.
Customers affected by a confirmed breach are informed within 48 hours of confirmation unless their contract sets a shorter period.
Good-faith reporting of an incident does not lead to disciplinary action, whereas failure to report will.
The incident log is kept 3 years, and S1 and S2 incidents get a post-incident review within 5 working days.
File shares and mailboxes are backed up daily at 23:00, kept 30 days for daily copies and 12 months for monthly copies, with restore tests every 6 months.
Remote access is through the Company VPN only with split tunnelling disabled.
Under the clean-desk rule customer documents must be locked away when leaving a desk for more than 30 minutes, and shredding collects on the first Wednesday of every month.
The security awareness course takes 45 minutes, must be completed within 30 days of joining and then yearly, with a target completion rate of 98%.
Phishing simulations run quarterly with a target click rate below 6%, and three simulated clicks within 12 months trigger one-to-one coaching with the ISO.
A policy exception must be approved by the ISO and the CTO and is valid for at most 6 months.
The policy is reviewed every 12 months or sooner after an S1 incident, and the next scheduled review is in June 2025.
Version 3.1 was approved by the Management Board on 24 June 2024 and is effective 1 July 2024.
The policy was approved by Marta Kowarzik, CEO, on behalf of the Management Board.
The security policy applies at all five depots, at the registered office, in the field and at home.
Company backups are copied off-site to Lintu Cloud Hosting and encrypted.
